hints: Look at each diagram and first spot which two resistors share the same two junction dots and so are in parallel.
Recall that for two resistors in parallel $1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$, and that this $R_p$ then adds directly to any resistor in series with the combination.
Work out the parallel part first in $\Omega$, then add the series resistor and check which total equals $100\,\Omega$.
walkthrough: Identify the arrangement in each circuit: A and B each have one resistor in series with a parallel pair, C has all three in parallel, and D has all three in series.
For a parallel pair use $1/R_p = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$. For two equal $100\,\Omega$ resistors, $1/R_p = 1/100 + 1/100 = 2/100$, so $R_p = 50\,\Omega$.
For a $100\,\Omega$ with a $50\,\Omega$ in parallel, $1/R_p = 1/100 + 1/50 = 3/100$, so $R_p = 33.3\,\Omega$.
Add any series resistor with $R_T = R_{series} + R_p$. In the circuit with $50\,\Omega$ in series with the $100\,\Omega$-$100\,\Omega$ parallel pair, $R_T = 50 + 50 = 100\,\Omega$.
The other totals are about $133\,\Omega$ for the $100\,\Omega$ series case, $25\,\Omega$ for three in parallel, and $250\,\Omega$ for three in series. This is option B.

options.A: The $100\,\Omega$ and $50\,\Omega$ are in parallel, giving about $33.3\,\Omega$, in series with $100\,\Omega$ for about $133\,\Omega$.
options.B: The two $100\,\Omega$ resistors in parallel give $50\,\Omega$, in series with $50\,\Omega$ for a total of $100\,\Omega$.
options.C: All three resistors $100\,\Omega$, $100\,\Omega$ and $50\,\Omega$ are in parallel, giving a combined resistance of $25\,\Omega$.
options.D: All three resistors are in series, so the total is $100+100+50 = 250\,\Omega$.
